title: Astro Design System Architecture Map
description: Canonical semantic index of the current Astro/Figma framework and the proposed architecture observability layer. It references existing authorities without replacing them.

architectureStates.title: Verified Current State
architectureStates.description: Observed repository behavior and ownership captured before architecture simplification.

architectureStates.title: Target Architecture Control Layer
architectureStates.description: A compact semantic graph, generated projections, focused lookup, and deterministic audits. It does not change component APIs, tokens, Figma, or brand output.

currentStateGaps: No ready page-template catalog exists. The only public template-layer record is SwiperStarter, which is a media starter rather than a page template.
D2 SVG generation depends on the local D2 CLI and remains reproducible from the semantic graph.
Workflow routing is documented across several files but was not previously represented as one queryable graph.

metadata.problem: Current behavior must remain distinguishable from proposed simplification.
Target controls must be reviewed without rewriting current-state evidence.
Work begins with human intent and may require explicit approval.
The executor needs explicit routing and terminal-output contracts.
Prompts vary from direct reuse to brand-sensitive creation.
Project-specific decisions cannot be inferred from neutral starter examples.
Reference traits require explicit adopt, avoid, rights, and approval evidence.
Agents need one entrypoint that routes only to relevant rule packs.
Different prompts should not incur the same context and validation cost.
Existing components and tokens must be checked before creation.
Page and section composition must report missing project inputs instead of inventing audience, content, offer, or information architecture.
Fast reuse must skip the brand system while creative brand work must activate it.
The starter contract is not-configured and cannot authorize production visual direction.
A new component is justified only by a reusable gap, not a local visual variation.
Work must not advance beyond checkpoints that require acceptance.
New component development must remain frozen while current architecture is inventoried and reviewed.
Agents should retrieve one relevant component or workflow instead of loading complete catalogs.
Ready assets need a preferred composition path that preserves child ownership.
Executable contracts must be changed in code before representations.
Documentation must mirror executable code and operational rules.
Runtime and responsive behavior cannot be validated from source or Figma alone.
Subjective visual direction requires evidence, a bounded pilot, and human judgment.
Figma must mirror accepted public contracts without becoming executable API truth.
Ready status requires aligned code, docs, browser evidence, Figma parity, audits, and checkpoints.
A new project needs an explicit fork boundary so framework foundations and project-owned context do not become mixed.
A duplicated Figma file needs project ownership while preserving stable registry identity and code-first mapping.
A queryable catalog is required for discovery, but it does not own executable API behavior.
Executable component behavior needs one production authority.
Shared design values require one code-owned authority.
Delivery scope and status require one auditable authority.
Project visual intent must be explicit, evidence-backed, and approved.
Reusable visual-design knowledge must remain separate from project direction.
Intentional code-to-Figma differences need explicit adapters.
Documentation mirrors code and provides usage context, but does not own API truth.
All reusable UI layers depend on stable foundations.
Small public primitives form the first reusable component layer.
Compact compositions reuse atoms across families.
Complex repeatable parts need private reusable masters without inflating public component count.
Cards are a cross-layer composition tier between small parts and larger regions.

nodes.title: Organisms and Sections (62 public; 35 sections ready)

The current registry has one media template but no ready page-template catalog.
Rendered behavior needs a real runtime surface.
Designers need an editable representation that preserves code-first identity.
Repository work requires inspect, patch, audit, and build operations.
Automated technical parity cannot judge subjective visual quality.
Figma family work pauses at stable review checkpoints.
Public files and registry records must remain one-to-one.
Family-specific contracts need checks beyond registry existence.
Foundation code, documentation, and mapping contracts must stay aligned.
Roadmap state must correspond to checks, dependencies, and evidence.
An empty starter must not silently become an approved brand.
Operational rules require deterministic structural validation.
Structural changes need executable project verification.
Every implementation workflow needs a concrete runtime result.
Synchronization needs a named terminal representation and evidence.
Workflows need explicit terminal output instead of silent completion.
A page or section prompt must stop with an explicit request when required audience, content, offer, or information-architecture input is missing.
A proven reusable component gap must be reported without silently bypassing the active architecture-phase component freeze.
Brand-sensitive production work must stop when visual direction is unapproved or outside the contract propagation scope.
The project needs an explicit output boundary separate from the reusable starter foundation.
Architecture knowledge needs one semantic, machine-readable index without competing with concern-specific authorities.

projectionPolicy.FigJam: optional presentation or workshop projection, never canonical
projectionPolicy.React Flow and ELK: deferred interactive explorer option, not part of this phase

Humans need durable visual projections while JSON remains canonical.

workflows.title: Use an Existing Ready Button
workflows.description: Resolve Button through focused lookup, read its actual API, import it, run a targeted structural check, and stop without loading brand-expression context.

steps.title: Receive the Button reuse prompt
Classify as Fast Reuse
Resolve the ready Button record and source
Import and compose Button in the target Astro file
Use repository discovery and patch tools
Run a targeted Astro check or build when imports changed
Report the reused component and validation result
steps.terminalOutput: Target file, Button API used, and targeted validation result.

validators.when: An Astro import, prop, or syntax boundary changed.
validators.reason: The edit must compile; unrelated family and brand audits are unnecessary.

toolCalls: npm run check or npm run build when warranted
duplicatedChecks: Button readiness can be checked in both the component registry and roadmap; Fast Reuse should prefer the registry and avoid reading the full roadmap.

metadata.brandPolicy: Fast Reuse must not load the full Brand Expression system.

workflows.title: Build a Page from Ready Sections or Templates
workflows.description: Use project context and the ready section catalog to compose a page. Current state has no page-template catalog, so page templates cannot be assumed.

steps.title: Receive the page-composition prompt
Classify as Guided Composition
Read populated project context or report the input gap
steps.condition: Page composition requires audience, content, offer, or IA input; do not infer it.

steps.title: Resolve only relevant ready sections
Compose the page route with canonical sections
Validate Astro and inspect the page in the browser
Report page composition, gaps, and validation
steps.terminalOutput: Page route, selected section identities, explicit content gaps, and build/browser result.

validators.when: A page route or Astro import is created or changed.

duplicatedChecks: Section readiness appears in the component registry, roadmap, website-section adapter, and website-section audit. Focused selection should read the registry first and the roadmap only for target/checkpoint state.

metadata.currentStateGap: No ready page-template catalog exists; SwiperStarter is not a page template.
metadata.brandPolicy: Load Brand Expression only when the requested page composition is brand-sensitive.

workflows.title: Build a New Section from Existing Components
workflows.description: Establish a reusable section role, compose ready child components, update registry/docs/roadmap, validate, and synchronize only after Astro acceptance.

steps.title: Receive the reusable section prompt
Route layout, component, project-context, and section rules
Confirm a reusable section-role gap
Read selected child component APIs and relevant project context
Create the section and update registry, docs, roadmap, and adapter
Run component, website-section, roadmap, and build validation
Report section contract and validation state
steps.terminalOutput: Section role, child dependencies, files written, checks run, browser evidence, and remaining Figma checkpoint.

validators.when: A public component or registry record is added.
validators.reason: Public source and registry identity must remain one-to-one.

validators.when: A website section or its documentation/adapter changes.
validators.reason: The section family contract must remain valid.

validators.when: Roadmap scope, dependencies, evidence, or status changes.
validators.reason: Roadmap truth must match implementation evidence.

validators.when: Astro source, imports, or documentation routes change.

humanApprovals: Family checkpoint after the eventual Figma representation
duplicatedChecks: Registry/file parity is checked by component architecture and website-section audits.
Roadmap evidence and section readiness are checked by both roadmap and website-section audits.

metadata.brandPolicy: If the section introduces brand-sensitive visual direction, branch through the approved Brand Expression gate before implementation.

workflows.title: Create a Genuinely Missing Component
workflows.description: Prove a reusable gap, establish atomic layer and family ownership, implement code-first, document, validate, and defer Figma until Astro acceptance.

steps.title: Receive the new-component prompt
Route framework, component, family, and mapping rules
Prove reuse gap and evaluate brand sensitivity
steps.condition: Creation is deferred while the architecture freeze is active; brand-sensitive creation also requires an approved contract.

steps.title: Implement source, tokens only if justified, registry, docs, roadmap, and adapter
Validate behavior and responsive states in the browser
Run only affected architecture, family, foundation, roadmap, and build checks
Report component acceptance and remaining parity work
steps.terminalOutput: Gap evidence, public API, ownership, writes, validators, browser result, and Figma synchronization status.

validators.when: A public source and registry record are added.
validators.reason: Identity and baseline invariants must remain valid.

validators.when: The affected family has a dedicated audit.
validators.reason: Family contracts must be tested without running unrelated family audits.

validators.when: Foundation tokens, styles, documentation, or mappings changed.
validators.reason: Do not run the foundation audit for a component-only change.

validators.when: Scope, dependencies, evidence, or status changed.
validators.reason: Roadmap state must match the new component lifecycle.

validators.when: Structural Astro or documentation changes were made.
validators.reason: The new public API must compile.

duplicatedChecks: Public source presence and sourcePath uniqueness recur across component, family, and roadmap audits.
Documentation evidence recurs across family and roadmap audits.

metadata.brandPolicy: Creative Creation must activate and respect approved brand rules whenever the result is brand-sensitive.

workflows.title: Redesign or Extend an Existing Component for a New Brand
workflows.description: Activate the complete brand-expression gate, calibrate a bounded representative component set, obtain human approval, and propagate only within the approved scope.

steps.title: Receive the brand-sensitive redesign prompt
Route framework, component, art-direction, brand, and family rules
Validate approved contract, references, boundaries, and propagation scope
Create a bounded browser or Figma calibration pilot
Obtain human visual approval
Update approved tokens, Astro components, docs, and mapping contract
Run brand, affected foundation/family, browser, and build checks
Report approval evidence and bounded propagation
steps.terminalOutput: Contract status, reference evidence, pilot result, human approval, propagation scope, files changed, and validation.

validators.when: Any brand-expression artifact or brand-sensitive production direction is involved.
validators.reason: The activation state and evidence contract must be valid.

validators.when: Approved shared values or foundation mappings changed.
validators.reason: Token truth must match docs and mappings.
Family API and representation contracts must remain valid.

duplicatedChecks: Brand activation and router linkage are checked by both brand-expression and agentic-rules audits.
Token mapping evidence can be checked by foundation, family, and roadmap audits.

metadata.brandPolicy: This workflow must never bypass the approved contract or human visual-quality gate.

workflows.title: Synchronize an Accepted Astro Component to Figma
workflows.description: Read code-first identity and API, inspect the exact Figma target, update idempotently, validate parity, record evidence, and stop at the family checkpoint.

steps.title: Receive the synchronization prompt
Route Figma2Astro and family rules
Read roadmap, registry identity, source API, tokens, and adapter
Inspect exact Figma page, master, variables, properties, and plugin-data identity
Create or repair the Figma representation idempotently
Validate properties, bindings, nested instances, parity, and roadmap evidence
Present one family checkpoint for acceptance
Report node IDs, intentional differences, checks, and checkpoint status
steps.terminalOutput: Figma file/page/master IDs, mapping evidence, intentional differences, parity result, roadmap write, and human checkpoint.

validators.when: A Figma master, property, binding, adapter, or family evidence changes.
validators.reason: The exact family contract and parity requirements must pass.

validators.when: Figma node IDs, evidence, checks, or status change.
validators.reason: Roadmap release truth must match the accepted representation.

humanApprovals: One family checkpoint after structural validation
duplicatedChecks: Master identity and parity evidence can be repeated in the family adapter, roadmap, and family audit.
Registry name/source identity and roadmap component identity overlap but own different concerns.

metadata.sourceOfTruthPolicy: Figma is the editable representation; Astro source remains executable API truth.

views.title: Framework Context (L0) — Current
views.description: Current actors, routing, concern-specific authorities, implementation surfaces, validation, and outputs.

views.title: Framework Context (L0) — Target Control Layer
views.description: Proposed architecture graph, focused tracer, deterministic audit, and generated D2 projections layered over the frozen current state.

views.title: Input-to-Output Pipeline (L1)
views.description: Primary decision path from prompt through reuse or creation, conditional brand calibration, code, browser, Figma, and terminal outputs.

views.title: Prompt → Astro Page or Section
views.description: Current prompt-to-Astro routing for page composition and reusable sections, including project-context gaps, focused component discovery, the conditional Brand Expression path, the architecture-phase creation freeze, validation, rework, and terminal handoff.

metadata.examplePrompt: Create a slider section using SectionHeader, Swiper, and Blog Cards.
metadata.contextCost: Low for ready reuse, medium for page composition, high for a reusable section, and very high only when approved brand calibration is activated.
metadata.scopeBoundary: Figma synchronization is a separate downstream workflow and is intentionally not part of this Astro acceptance view.

views.title: Fast Reuse Mode
views.description: Focused ready-Button trace with explicit Brand Expression exclusions.

views.title: Guided Composition Mode
views.description: Page composition from ready sections with project-context gating and the current page-template gap.

views.title: Creative Creation and Extension Mode
views.description: Genuine component creation with conditional brand activation and code-first acceptance.

views.title: Existing Component Repair
views.description: Repair path that resolves code truth, updates mirrored artifacts, validates runtime, and synchronizes accepted changes.

views.title: Component Lifecycle and Release
views.description: Discovery, implementation, documentation, browser evidence, Figma parity, human checkpoint, roadmap, and release.

views.title: Astro ↔ Figma Identity and Mapping
views.description: Code-first identity, registry indexing, adapters, editable Figma representation, parity validation, and accepted output.

views.title: New Project Fork and Duplicated Figma File Flow
views.description: A project fork supplies its own context and brand contract while preserving stable framework identities and creating a project-owned Figma representation.

metadata.currentEvidenceLimit: The repository documents new-project brand calibration and Figma mapping, but no executable duplicated-Figma-file automation was found.

views.title: Brand Expression and Art Direction Calibration
views.description: Conditional evidence, approval, calibration, implementation, and propagation path.

views.title: Sources of Truth by Concern
views.description: Non-competing concern ownership: registry for discovery/identity, Astro for API/runtime, CSS for values, contract for visual intent, roadmap for status, adapters for representation differences, Figma for editable representation, and the graph for architecture indexing.

views.title: Atomic Design Dependency View
views.description: Foundation-to-page dependency order with explicit current inventory counts and the missing page-template catalog.

views.title: Brand-Sensitive Component Extension
views.description: Complete creative calibration trace including contract and human approval gates.

views.title: Accepted Astro to Figma Synchronization
views.description: Code-first synchronization trace with tool calls, parity checks, roadmap evidence, and family acceptance.
